“Shield Hero, come to think of it, what are you doing for Valentine’s Day?”
“Valentine’s Day? Come to think of it, the merchants were talking about that. Does that exist in this world, too?”
“Yes. My family runs a chocolate farm, and since they’ve been helping us out in various ways, I thought it might be useful…”
“Your family runs a chocolate farm!?”
…A chocolate farm. What an amazing phrase. Is it a family that makes chocolate? In that case, wouldn’t they be called pastry chefs? No, wait—pastry chefs are confectioners, aren’t they? So, it must be some kind of guild or organization that specializes in making chocolate. I brushed it off at the time, but once I arrived at the village, I concluded there must be trees that bear chocolate.
…Still, those farmers must be at high risk for diabetes.
“I hated working on the chocolate farm, so I ran away from home dreaming of becoming an adventurer… only to end up as a thief.”
Huh… It’s a pretty common storyline—the classic story of someone who had a dream but failed. He mentioned going back home to take over the family business, but what’s it like to take over a chocolate farm? I couldn’t help but think it might actually be kind of fun.
“Lately, I’ve been keeping in touch with my family by letter. I told them, ‘If the Shield Hero wants some chocolate, maybe they’d be willing to buy some?’ I could even act as a go-between.”
“Hmm… I’ll think about it.”
“And… about my dad…”
The Robin Hood-type muttered, then looked away.
“If possible, please negotiate only with my sister and mom. If you take this letter to them, I think they’ll agree! ”
“Ah, uh…”
---
And that’s how I ended up getting a letter of introduction to a chocolate farm from the Robin Hood. Demand for chocolate is high this season, so prices are on the high side. That said, there’s no real benefit to storing chocolate long-term in my village. I could buy it during the off-season and freeze it with Magic, but that would mean waiting until next year. Apparently, last year’s harvest was poor due to the waves, and prices are on the rise this year.
So… the chocolate farm is located in a colder region, just a short distance from the former territory of Melromarc. If chocolate trees grew in a warm climate, they’d probably just melt, after all… It’s February now, and the fact that they’re harvested during the cold season makes sense, all things considered.
“I’m starting to smell something sweet.”
“Yeah, I do, too.”
As we traveled by carriage, a gradually cloying scent began to waft through the air. It wasn’t just the smell of chocolate—it was simply a sweet smell. It’s a scent I’m not very familiar with. Even in the real world, there probably aren’t many places where you’d smell something like this. Wait a minute. Maybe this is the kind of smell you’d find at a candy factory?
By the way, I’d noticed along the way that quite a lot of chocolate was being sold in the markets due to Valentine’s Day demand. This world really loves its events, doesn’t it?
…Come to think of it, the tradition was originally spread by the Hero, wasn’t it? Has it become a religious observance as well? If every household were required to buy chocolate, well, that would certainly create demand and help the custom take root. Even the accessory merchant’s chain stores were selling chocolate accessories.
What’s the deal with decorating yourself with food? For starters, you shouldn’t be messing around with food… That’s what I think, but I guess that’s just how vibrant the market has become.
“So… where are the farmers who sell chocolate?”
“Hm? Oh, hold on a sec.”
When Raphtalia asked me, I checked the map included with the letter of introduction from the Robin Hood-like figure.
“It’s over there.”
There were tons of chocolate farms… We made our way through a dense grove of chocolate trees. Just seeing this made me feel conflicted. I’d actually seen a real chocolate tree.
The chocolate bars grew in clusters, much like bananas. It was a fantastical sight. Or rather, was it more like a fairy tale? The shape was different from that of a bread tree, too.
The bread trees in my village don’t have those crepe-like, pitcher-plant-style parts. They seem to bear fruit simply from the nutrients they absorb through their roots. At the tip of each bread fruit is a jam-like part that acts like a seed; if you plant it, a new tree sprouts in a matter of days. It’s quite the monster tree, isn’t it?
It could solve our food problem in one fell swoop. The problem is… as Rat’s investigation revealed, it causes significant damage to the soil. If we don’t manage it properly, we could end up with crop rotation problems and barren land in the blink of an eye. We’ve left this area to the Dune and Rumo folks to handle. As a worst-case scenario, we’re securing land to clear and let it rest. Since it’s essentially a bio-plant, as long as we have the seeds, it’ll be fine in a few days.
Anyway, the chocolate tree had chocolate caked all over its trunk. “Why is it stuck on there like this?” I wondered as I approached the trunk—and then I understood. A small, insect-like monster was clinging to the trunk, already dead. This part of the tree is probably similar in structure to the crepe tree.
I wonder if it’s sucking the nutrients out of the insects, too? What a gross tree…
“Lord Naofumi. It looks like there are other kinds of trees besides the chocolate ones?”
I looked in the direction Raphtalia was pointing and noticed trees that looked like candy and others that looked like marshmallows. Is this place Sweets Land or something?!
“A-anyway… let’s head to the chocolate farm.”
The chocolate farmers must be in their busy season too; they were frantically gathering the ripe chocolate and preparing shipments. Farmers had also come to the chocolate tree I’d been watching and were picking the chocolate. So, I decided to ask them while I was there.
“Hey.”
“Yes?”
The chocolate farmer—who didn’t seem to know I was the Shield Hero—turned around with a annoyed expression after being addressed in the middle of his busy work.
“Do you know how to get to this farm?”
“Oh, you mean Rō-boy’s place?”
The farmer, who’d looked like he was annoyed I’d interrupted him while he was busy, now gave me a sympathetic look. What’s up? Is there some kind of problem? If so, I’d have to mete out some justice to those Robin Hood types…
“Well, you’ll have to go straight through town first, then follow the road all the way east. If possible, you should just talk to Rou-bou’s mother and sister. Everyone’s been worried because they’re probably having a hard time over there, too.”
“Huh…”
I wonder… it feels like the kind of place where they’d try to palm me off with some shoddy goods.
“That place… the quality’s actually pretty good, though…”
He must have sensed my thoughts and decided to fill me in. Or rather, is it okay for him to interrupt his work like this? The other merchants are glaring at us, you know? The guys who approach me, looking annoyed, nod as if they understand when the one I spoke to points east. …I’m starting to feel really uneasy.
“Want me to show you the way?”
“No, you’re probably busy, so I don’t want to trouble you that much.”
“Is that so? Well, is there anything else you’re curious about?”
“If you’re hiding something, tell me.”
“Well… you’ll see when you get there. I’d rather not say any more than that… It’s not like we’re ostracizing anyone or anything, though.”
So they’re not hiding anything… but this is really killing my desire to buy.
“Anything else?”
“Once the chocolate is harvested, when will it bear fruit again?”
“At this time of year, it bears fruit quickly—in a month. That’s when the white chocolate will be ready. After that season passes, it’ll be four months.”
White chocolate… so there’s a White Day, too. I’d better be prepared.
Normally it’s a four-month cycle, but does growth speed up as Valentine’s Day approaches? It really is different from the trees back home. Whether it’s the bread tree or the crepe tree, they bear fruit year-round. Is it the difference in the soil…? I wonder what they’re originally made of?
“A Chocolate Monster has appeared!”
Just as we were talking about that, a sludge-like, chocolate-shaped monster appeared.

“Well, we’ve taken care of that idiot. Let’s get back to the business talks.”
“Yeah, you’re right.”
“You’re so kind, Shield Hero.”
What’s so kind about that? I just blew your dad right out of here. Anyway, these guys are really light. That guy must be the cause of all this.
“Aaaah…”
Raphtalia is speechless. These guys are the ones who’re just letting it slide, aren’t they?
“Gwaaaaah! What the hell are you doing all of a sudden?!”
A figure bursts out of the chocolate swamp with a splash. Tsk! Did I miss my shot?
That’s exactly what I’d say. Tearing up someone’s letter of introduction out of the blue like that. One wrong move and that’s a crime. That’s how valuable a letter of introduction can be, depending on the person. I glare at the Robin Hood-like father while clicking my tongue.
“If you want my chocolate, prove your love for it.”
“Hmph!”
I stomp on a piece of chocolate lying nearby and kick it away. I hate guys who spout this kind of nonsensical nonsense the most. Part of the reason is that it reminds me of those heroes from before, but I just can’t stand people I can’t reason with. You could even say I loathe them. What’s this “love for chocolate” nonsense? There’s no such thing!
“You there! Get lost! I’m not giving you any chocolate!”
“That’s none of my business. I’m not buying from you. I’m buying from those two over there.”
“What did you say?!”
“To be honest, I don’t even want to know how twisted your so-called ‘love for chocolate’ really is.”
“You said it! Well then, let me show you the results of my research! You’ll be in agony once you experience my love!”
How did it come to this? I told you I didn’t want to know. Seriously, I honestly don’t want to know.
You can tell at a glance that he’s a researcher type, like Rat. But he’s not a level-headed person like Rat, is he? …Even though he’s become a bit of a caveman due to his fieldwork, he did understand what I said, right? It’s more troublesome when a conversation can’t hold together even though we should be able to understand each other. In that regard, Raph-chan is great. She picks up on my intentions even when we don’t speak the same language.
The Robin Hood-type old man staggers out of the swamp and slowly beckons me toward the field. I stride over to the field with an air of superiority.
“Watch this! My invention!”
Saying things like that, the Robin Hood-type old man digs up a potato-like vegetable buried in the field. His words and actions don’t match up.
“Here! Try it!”
I wasn’t exactly thrilled to be handed a vegetable, but when I saw what he’d tossed my way, I was taken aback. It was pitch-black… truffle chocolate.
“Well, what do you think? It’s one of my inventions: ‘Truffle Chocolate That Grows in the Field’!”
Is this some kind of cooking manga full of things to make fun of?! I shoved the truffle chocolate into my mouth and ate it. The quality wasn’t too bad, but of course, it tasted like dirt.
“Well? Your so-called love for chocolate is nothing in front of me! Everyone who fails to appreciate me is just foolish!”
“I was wondering what you were going to say—‘love’? No matter what it is, without supply and demand, it’s as good as nothing. Know this: self-indulgent inventions are the most meaningless of all!”
“What did you say?!”
O Robin Hood. I understand all too well why you ran away from home. If you had parents who thought you were some kind of genius capable of making a great invention—that’s just pathetic—you’d want to escape, too.
“Let me point out the flaw in this truffle chocolate! It’s that it’s hard to tell the difference between the dirt and the cocoa powder! Customers want chocolate—they don’t want to eat dirt!”
In fact, the truffle chocolate I ate had the dirt asserting itself very strongly amidst the cocoa powder flavor. But removing the dirt inevitably means removing the cocoa powder along with it. Washing it with water would only make the problem worse. I doubt anyone would want to eat truffle chocolate that’s been soaked in water. To begin with, water and chocolate are a terrible combination.
“And by the way, are you trying to say that ‘chocolate’ equals ‘truffle chocolate’? Besides, isn’t this just a subspecies of the chocolate tree? Love? That’s exactly what’s missing.”
The direction of his passion for breeding isn’t entirely wrong, but to call this “complete” at this stage is laughable. If this truffle chocolate had grown on a tree, it might have been passable. If it were a finished truffle chocolate from the start, there’d be no need for all this processing. If that were the case, I could say it had some potential.
“Let him say whatever he wants! Well then, let’s take a look at the next one!”
“Ah… It seems a contest of some sort has begun between Naofumi-sama and me.”
Raphtalia muttered in a fed-up tone. I don’t know about that. I’ve got to knock some sense into a cocky guy like this—otherwise, my business spirit won’t settle down. Let’s punish this guy who’s completely underestimated the business!
“Here’s the next one!”
The Robin Hood-type old man pointed to one of the fruits on the chocolate tree—a banana-like one—ripped it off, and tossed it at me.
“It’s just a banana! I mean, do bananas even exist in this world?”
That’s beside the point. Do bananas even exist…? Come to think of it, I think there was banana whipped cream on the crepe tree…?
“Hmph. That’s why you lack love! To think you can’t see my love. Go ahead and peel it!”
I peel the banana as instructed… and the inside turns out to be chocolate. I don’t get it.
“This is one of my finest inventions: the ‘Chocolate Banana That Grows on Trees’!”
Wait, doesn’t chocolate in this world already grow on trees? And anyway, banana peels are yellow—I wonder if, just like a real banana, the chocolate gets sweeter as it ripens.
…I take a bite. It’s just chocolate shaped like a banana. It’s not like the chocolate bananas you get at night markets. In fact, it’s not even banana-flavored chocolate. It’s just chocolate shaped like a banana. This is no different from chocolate wrapped in silver foil. Maybe the gimmick could sell it, but it’s a bit of a gimmick for kids.
“How foolish… This falls far short of what you’d call a chocolate banana. You’ve simply wrapped chocolate in a banana peel and made it ‘grow’ on a tree.”
“You… you wretch! To deny my love… Get out! Get out!”
“You kick people out the moment you realize they don’t understand you? You’re really taking the customer service business for granted.”
“My invention is something that those with an eye for it will understand! After I’m gone, future generations will come to love and nurture the inventions I’ve created! Yes, the times just haven’t caught up yet!”
“I was wondering what you were going to say… This isn’t a painting, you know? If you’re that passive, there’s no way you’ll sell anything!”
In my world, there are stories about famous painters—like the one known for sunflowers—who barely sold anything during their lifetimes. So, people who aren’t recognized tend to compare themselves to these famous painters and rant about how they’ll be appreciated by future generations!
But actually being recognized is the rare exception! There are people who work thousands of times harder than those who get recognized later, yet they fade into obscurity without ever being appreciated. Those cases are just a tiny, tiny fraction of the exceptions.
In reality, the fact that that painter’s works started fetching high prices was largely due to a shrewd merchant. He raised the value of a massive pile of Trash—which was originally practically worthless—and sold it. In that sense, while the painter who kept churning out work in large quantities was impressive, that merchant was even more so.
To begin with, if someone isn’t recognized for their work and ends up neglecting to even publish it, there’s no way anything decent could come out of some weird invention they come up with in a place like this. A hidden genius? An invention that gets recognized only after the developer’s death? Give me a break! Think about those of us who have to put up with the pathetic delusions of aspiring artists!
“I do think the invention itself is amazing, but… this…”
Raphtalia looks troubled as she samples this jerk of a dad’s invention. You don’t have to eat this piece of junk.
“That’s right. My husband is the type who’s always coming up with weird inventions…”
“Yeah. Dad says he’ll never sell his chocolate to anyone who doesn’t understand it, so our finances are in shambles… and to top it off, he keeps getting swindled by shady salesmen.”
“He’s being sweet-talked, isn’t he?”
The Robin Hood’s mother and sister nodded. That’s it. They’ll use some excuse like “sales cooperation” and end up selling it for a song. Since the quality is only halfway decent, they might actually melt down the contents and turn it into a different product. It just occurred to me… but that’s exactly the kind of trick the merchants I know would pull.
“You’re eating—besides the chocolate—the sweet lies that those who try to deceive you spout. Did it taste good?”
“But what you need to do is abandon your dreams—which are sweeter than real chocolate—and face the bitter… no, the dark chocolate reality head-on.”
“Grrr… I won’t forgive you! I won’t forgive you! Just you wait and see my great invention with your own eyes!”
“You’re still at it… but the caliber of your invention is nothing to write home about.”
The Robin Hood-like thief’s father turned bright red and ran off toward the workshop, where the smoke had cleared.

The good-for-nothing dad of the Robin Hood-like thief runs toward the workshop. I follow slowly behind him. Then I take a look inside the workshop.
It has a different vibe from Rat’s lab. Well, that place prioritizes monster research, so it’s more of a proper research facility. “I can understand why he’d prioritize his appetite over his instincts. Either way, confessing to a dragon is pretty weird… Well, Gaelion is totally devoted to Naofumi, though.”
“Cut it out. You’re going to make my trauma flare up again.”
“Okay, okay. Naofumi, why don’t you be supportive—or better yet, encourage him?”
Come to think of it, she’s right. If that mutant can keep Gaelion tied up, that’d be a huge win. In fact, whether it’s a fait accompli or whatever, I should make Gaelion doubt himself—create an excuse to reject him later, saying, ‘I absolutely won’t date someone who isn’t devoted to me!’
“Go for it! Seduce that gay dragon!”
“Naofumi-sama, please support me in your heart.”
“C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C-C Hah… Who’s going to save him, you fool!”
“Well, it’ll probably be good therapy for his body… but a hybrid of a Filolial and a new species of monster—that’s quite a strange combination.”
Even Gaelion’s parent seems to have given up on him somewhat.
“Kueh!”
The mutant is clamping down on Gaelion’s tail right at the base and sucking on it. Is this some kind of kink? Gaelion looks like he’s desperately trying to hold back. Even Taniko—who, as expected, knows about Gaelion’s perverted tastes—isn’t saying anything. She looks like she’s just hoping this rough treatment will make him stop targeting me.
Hm? I spot a rare guy watching the scene with flames of jealousy rising in his eyes. The Thoroughbred is staring at Gaelion and the mutant from the shadows of the building. But his gaze is seriously scary. Since this one is a Filolial, Gaelion should be genetically repulsed by it. So… wait? Does that guy actually like the mutant?
I’d forgotten, but the Thoroughbred is male and the mutant is female. So when he’d been eyeing her as a Rival, was he actually just interested and trying to tease her? He’s just as much of a pain in the neck as his foster parent. He’s so fast, he must be a total heartthrob… so why on earth is he falling for that high-maintenance one? And on top of that, even after nearly getting eaten by her, he still likes her?
Come to think of it, for Filolials, showing that you’re superior to your partner is part of their courtship behavior. In other words, since this guy takes pride in his speed, he had to outrun the Variant.
Yeah. Children take after their parents. It’s all well and good to analyze it that way, but by that logic, that guy and I would end up being similar. Let me just say right now: I’m not like that. In my case, I’ll just chalk it up to how I was raised.
“CUREEEEEEEEEEE!”
Gaelion’s scream echoed through the village. Just as… White Day was drawing to a close.
“Hey.”
Taniko beckoned me over.
“Big bro!”
And Keel, too, for good measure.
“What’s up?”
“Well, you see. The Chocolate Monster that Wyndia-chan was taking care of—”
“I told you to get rid of it if it caused any trouble, didn’t I?”
“No… it says it wants to talk to you.”
Talk? I don’t have anything to talk about. I don’t even have anything to talk about in the first place. But if I just leave it alone, who knows what trouble it might cause. Taniko pointed at the Chocolate Monster standing in front of the crepe tree and replied. I had all the heroes prepare for battle and stand by, ready to engage at any moment.
“What is it?”
I asked after we’d formed a perimeter. Then, a faint light began to rise from the Chocolate Monster.
“It’s about… time, apparently.”
“Time for what?”
“The Chocolate Monster is only around for a limited time, right? It’s saying that time is almost up.”
“So?”
I hold my shield out in front of me, fully prepared to run if anything happens, and stay on high alert. Taniko continues, her attitude making it obvious at a glance that she thinks I’m overreacting.
“It’s saying ‘goodbye’ because it’s about to disappear.”
The white Chocolate Monster is waving goodbye to me, the villagers, and Gaelion. I see. Go ahead and disappear already. With this, I can finally say goodbye to those days of living in fear of chocolate.
“I was able to spend a very meaningful and happy Valentine’s Day and White Day this year. Sure, I went a little too wild… but I’m grateful that, in all my time as a Chocolate Monster, I’ve never had such an active time as this.”
He’s trying to wrap this up as a heartwarming story, but I won’t forget. Because I ate Gaelion’s chocolate, I went on a rampage and tried to fulfill Gaelion’s wish! It’s all your fault I’ve been traumatized! One wrong move and I would’ve been impregnated!
The Chocolate Monster floated gently, glowing with a soft light as it became translucent and faded away. It kept staring at us as it headed toward the crepe tree, waving goodbye before flying off and disappearing.
“It said it’ll come back next year.”
“Don’t ever come back.”
“Naofumi-sama… I understand how you feel, but it’s such a beautiful sight…”
The light emitted by the Chocolate Monster rained down like snow all around us before fading away. The other heroes seemed captivated by the fantastical scene, but I couldn’t bring myself to enjoy it. The faint light formed a ribbon that tied together the hands of Itsuki and Rishia, who were happily holding hands, creating a scene reminiscent of a red thread before vanishing.
In Ren’s case, it was Taniko and the female knight. As for Motoyasu… the Filolials… the ribbon seemed to be floating above them cheerfully. He tried to reach out to Filo, but she dodged him.
And then… the light I’d scattered over the villagers gathered above me, took on some sort of shape, and fell right in front of my eyes. The light lingered there as if urging me to catch it… so I knocked it away.
“Naofumi-sama, please, just read the room and take it.”
“N-o-w-a-y! Who says I’m clueless?”
“Sigh… I knew it.”
Raphtalia picked it up and took my hand. Then—perhaps it was the villagers’ inner voices—even though no one was speaking, I could sense voices saying “thank you” and feelings of “I love you” coming through. Being thanked like that all over again makes me feel a little awkward. But I didn’t want to accept it through a phenomenon like this.
“But… why did it disappear toward the crepe tree?”
“I don’t know…”
I have a very bad feeling about this.
Some time later… I’ll note here that Keel came to report—as a truly trivial matter—that the crepe tree had become more powerful. Specifically, the taste of the chocolate sauce had improved, and the overall quality had gotten better. Also, the trunk had thickened, and it seems to be growing little by little. I’d hate for it to eventually grow as big as the World Tree, but I remember Keel saying his ambition was to make it a huge tree visible even from afar.
Another completely trivial note… the following year, the same chocolate monster—or so it seemed—appeared in my territory and spent some time in the village. To dispose of a monster that’s invulnerable even when blown to smithereens, you have to bend the laws of nature using the power of spirits—but the spirits wouldn’t… lend their power for something so trivial.
In a way, that creature is just like a spirit. What on earth is a chocolate spirit, anyway…?
Well, that’s more or less how Valentine’s Day and White Day passed by.
